questions.explanation: **Correct (A, B):** Rolling linens with the soiled side inward and holding them away from the uniform while placing them in the hamper without shaking keeps microorganisms from spreading to the aide or into the air. Why the others are wrong: **C** shaking linens releases pathogens into the air; **D** putting linens on the floor spreads contamination and is poor practice.

questions.stem: A resident is on airborne precautions for active tuberculosis. Which type of mask should the nurse aide wear when entering the room, per facility policy?

options.text: No mask is needed if the aide holds their breath
A loose paper towel held over the face
A fitted N95 respirator (or as the facility's policy specifies)
A cloth scarf tied around the nose

questions.explanation: **Correct (C):** Airborne precautions for tuberculosis require a fitted N95 respirator (or the respirator specified by facility policy) to filter the small airborne particles. Why the others are wrong: **A** holding one's breath is impossible and offers no protection; **B** a paper towel does not seal or filter airborne particles; **D** a cloth scarf is not a tested respirator and does not provide airborne protection.

questions.stem: A nurse aide takes an axillary (under-the-arm) temperature. Compared with an oral temperature, an axillary reading is generally:

options.text: About one degree Fahrenheit lower than oral
About one degree Fahrenheit higher than oral
Exactly the same as a rectal temperature
Always within the fever range

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** An axillary temperature reads roughly one degree Fahrenheit lower than an oral temperature taken at the same time, so the route is documented with the reading. Why the others are wrong: **B** axillary readings are lower, not higher, than oral; **C** rectal temperatures run about a degree higher than oral, so axillary is not the same as rectal; **D** an axillary reading reflects the resident's actual temperature and is not automatically a fever.

questions.stem: A nurse aide counts a resting radial pulse and notes it is regular. For how long should a regular pulse typically be counted to report a rate per minute accurately?

options.text: For 5 seconds, then multiply by 12
Only until the first beat is felt
For a full 60 seconds, or 30 seconds multiplied by 2 if the facility allows for a regular pulse
For 10 minutes to be thorough

questions.explanation: **Correct (C):** A regular pulse is counted for a full minute, or for 30 seconds and multiplied by two where policy allows; an irregular pulse is always counted for a full minute. Why the others are wrong: **A** a 5-second count is too brief to be reliable; **B** counting only the first beat gives no rate at all; **D** 10 minutes is unnecessary and impractical.

questions.stem: A resident on a bleeding-precaution care plan gets a small skin cut that is bleeding. While waiting for the nurse, what is the most appropriate first action for the aide?

options.text: Apply firm, direct pressure over the wound with a clean barrier while wearing gloves
Apply a tourniquet tightly above the cut
Leave the wound open to the air and walk away to find supplies
Rinse the cut with the resident's drinking water and ignore it

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** Bleeding from a minor wound is controlled by applying firm, direct pressure with a clean barrier while wearing gloves, and notifying the nurse. Why the others are wrong: **B** a tourniquet is for severe limb hemorrhage and can cause harm if misused; **C** leaving and abandoning the resident delays control of the bleeding; **D** rinsing with drinking water does not stop bleeding and ignoring it is unsafe.

questions.stem: A resident who is diabetic suddenly becomes shaky, sweaty, and confused before lunch. What should the nurse aide do?

options.text: Tell the resident to lie down and wait until the next scheduled meal
Encourage the resident to exercise to feel better
Notify the nurse immediately, because these can be signs of low blood sugar
Decide it is just hunger and take no action

questions.explanation: **Correct (C):** Shakiness, sweating, and new confusion in a diabetic resident can signal low blood sugar, which is reported to the nurse at once for evaluation and treatment. Why the others are wrong: **A** waiting for the next meal can allow a dangerous drop in blood sugar; **B** exercise lowers blood sugar further and worsens the problem; **D** dismissing the signs as hunger ignores a potential emergency.

questions.stem: A nurse aide applies anti-embolism (compression) stockings ordered to help prevent blood clots. Which two practices are correct? (Select two.)

options.text: Apply the stockings in the morning before the resident gets out of bed, while the legs are least swollen
Make sure the stockings are smooth and free of twists or wrinkles after application
Apply the stockings over a thick pair of socks for extra warmth
Roll or fold the top of the stocking down to make a snug band around the leg

questions.explanation: **Correct (A, B):** Applying the stockings before the resident rises (while the legs are least swollen) and keeping them smooth and wrinkle-free lets them deliver even compression without harming the skin. Why the others are wrong: **C** applying them over thick socks prevents proper compression and can bunch and irritate the skin; **D** rolling or folding the top creates a tight band that constricts circulation, the opposite of the intended effect.

questions.stem: A nurse aide is making an occupied bed for a resident who must stay in bed. Which two practices promote comfort and skin protection? (Select two.)

options.text: Keep the bottom sheet pulled tight and free of wrinkles and crumbs
Raise both side rails and leave the bed in its highest position when finished
Roll the resident toward the far side rail and keep them covered while changing the near half of the bed
Leave damp linens under the resident to save a second trip

questions.explanation: **Correct (A, C):** A taut, wrinkle- and crumb-free bottom sheet protects the skin from pressure and irritation, and turning the resident to one side while keeping them covered lets the aide change half the bed safely and with dignity. Why the others are wrong: **B** leaving the bed in its highest position when finished is a fall hazard; **D** leaving damp linens against the skin promotes breakdown and discomfort.

questions.stem: A nurse aide is collecting a routine (clean-catch) urine specimen as delegated. After the specimen is collected, how should it be handled?

options.text: Leave the open container at the bedside until the end of the shift
Pour part of it out so the lab does not get too much
Label the container with the resident's information, close it, and take it to the designated area promptly per policy
Carry the uncovered specimen in a bare hand to the nurse

questions.explanation: **Correct (C):** A specimen is correctly labeled with the resident's identifying information, sealed, and delivered promptly to the proper place so results are accurate and matched to the right resident. Why the others are wrong: **A** leaving an open specimen out allows contamination and degradation; **B** discarding part of the sample can compromise testing; **D** carrying an uncovered specimen in a bare hand is unsanitary and unsafe.

questions.stem: After people are safe and the alarm has sounded, a nurse aide uses a fire extinguisher on a small contained fire. Place the steps of the PASS technique in the correct order.

options.text: Pull the pin to unlock the extinguisher
Aim the nozzle at the base of the fire
Squeeze the handle to release the agent
Sweep the nozzle from side to side across the base of the fire

questions.explanation: The PASS technique is Pull, Aim, Squeeze, Sweep. The pin is pulled first to unlock the extinguisher so it can discharge. The nozzle is then aimed at the base of the fire, because the base is where the burning fuel is and where the agent must land to be effective. The handle is squeezed to release the extinguishing agent, and finally the nozzle is swept from side to side across the base to smother the flames. Aiming at the flames or smoke instead of the base would fail to put out the fire.

questions.stem: When applying a warm compress that the nurse has delegated, which observation should the nurse aide report promptly?

options.text: The resident says the warmth feels soothing
The compress cools to room temperature after several minutes
The skin under the compress becomes very red, blistered, or the resident reports burning pain
The resident relaxes and closes their eyes

questions.explanation: **Correct (C):** Excessive redness, blistering, or burning pain signals a possible burn or skin injury from heat and must be reported promptly (and the compress removed). Why the others are wrong: **A** soothing warmth is the expected effect; **B** a compress naturally cools over time, which is normal; **D** the resident relaxing is a sign the treatment is comfortable, not a problem.

questions.stem: A nurse aide measures a pulse oximetry reading on a resident's finger as delegated. The device shows a much lower reading than usual and the resident looks short of breath. What should the aide do?

options.text: Adjust the resident's oxygen flow rate to raise the number
Tell the resident to hold their breath to reset the device
Delete the reading because the machine must be broken
Report the low reading and the resident's shortness of breath to the nurse right away

questions.explanation: **Correct (D):** A low oxygen reading combined with shortness of breath is an abnormal finding the aide reports to the nurse immediately for assessment. Why the others are wrong: **A** changing the oxygen flow rate is the nurse's responsibility, not the aide's; **B** telling a short-of-breath resident to hold their breath is unsafe and does not address the problem; **C** discarding a possibly accurate reading hides a warning sign.

questions.stem: While performing active-assistive range-of-motion exercises, how far should the nurse aide move each joint?

options.text: Past the point of pain to gain more motion
Only a tiny amount, never near the joint's normal range
As fast and far as possible in one quick motion
Only to the point of slight resistance or mild discomfort, never forcing the joint

questions.explanation: **Correct (D):** Joints are moved slowly and smoothly to the point of slight resistance or mild discomfort and never forced, which safely maintains motion. Why the others are wrong: **A** moving past pain can injure the joint and tissues; **B** moving only a tiny amount fails to maintain the joint's normal range of motion; **C** fast, jerky movement risks injury.

questions.stem: A resident who had a stroke is learning to dress independently but is slow and fumbles with buttons. What approach best supports the resident's rehabilitation?

options.text: Take over and dress the resident every time to be efficient
Remove all buttoned clothing so the resident never practices
Tell the resident to give up and let staff handle dressing
Allow extra time, offer encouragement, and let the resident do what they can, assisting only as needed

questions.explanation: **Correct (D):** Restorative care builds independence by giving the resident time and encouragement to do as much as possible, with the aide assisting only where needed. Why the others are wrong: **A** taking over fosters dependence and undoes rehabilitation; **B** removing all practice opportunities prevents the resident from regaining the skill; **C** discouraging the resident harms motivation and recovery.

questions.stem: A resident uses a prosthetic leg. Before the resident puts it on, what skin-related observation should the nurse aide make and report if abnormal?

options.text: Whether the residual limb has any redness, sores, swelling, or skin breakdown
The exact brand name printed on the prosthesis
How much the prosthesis weighs in pounds
The color of the resident's shoe

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** The aide checks the residual (stump) limb for redness, sores, swelling, or breakdown before the prosthesis is applied and reports any abnormal skin findings to the nurse. Why the others are wrong: **B** the brand name has nothing to do with the resident's skin health; **C** the prosthesis weight is not a skin observation; **D** shoe color is irrelevant to skin integrity.

questions.stem: A resident with dementia is anxiously trying to fold towels over and over. The activity is harmless and keeps the resident calm. What should the nurse aide do?

options.text: Take the towels away and tell the resident to stop
Move the resident to a louder, busier area
Tell the resident the towels are already folded and to sit still
Allow the resident to continue the soothing, repetitive activity and offer gentle reassurance

questions.explanation: **Correct (D):** A harmless, repetitive activity that calms a resident with dementia should be allowed and supported with gentle reassurance, as it meets a need for purpose and reduces anxiety. Why the others are wrong: **A** taking the towels away can trigger agitation and removes a comforting activity; **B** moving the resident to a louder area increases overstimulation and anxiety; **C** insisting the resident sit still ignores the calming benefit.

questions.stem: A resident becomes verbally angry and shouts at the nurse aide over a minor delay. What is the most therapeutic initial response?

options.text: Shout back so the resident knows the aide is in charge
Threaten to report the resident for being difficult
Walk out and refuse to return for the rest of the shift
Stay calm, listen without arguing, and acknowledge the resident's frustration

questions.explanation: **Correct (D):** Remaining calm, listening without arguing, and acknowledging the feeling helps de-escalate anger and shows respect for the resident. Why the others are wrong: **A** shouting back escalates the conflict; **B** threatening the resident is intimidating and unprofessional; **C** abandoning the resident neglects their care and worsens trust.

questions.stem: A resident who recently moved into the facility says, 'I feel useless now that I can't do anything for myself.' Which response best supports the resident's self-esteem?

options.text: Agree that the resident cannot do much anymore
Do everything for the resident so they do not have to try
Tell the resident not to think about it
Acknowledge the feeling and encourage the resident to take part in care and choices they are still able to make

questions.explanation: **Correct (D):** Acknowledging the feeling and encouraging the resident to participate in care and make choices restores a sense of control and self-worth. Why the others are wrong: **A** agreeing that they are useless deepens low self-esteem; **B** doing everything for the resident reinforces helplessness rather than dignity; **C** dismissing the feeling shuts down the resident's expression.

questions.stem: A resident from a culture in which direct eye contact is considered disrespectful tends to look away when the nurse aide speaks. How should the aide interpret and respond to this?

options.text: Assume the resident is being rude and confront them
Recognize it as a cultural norm, respect it, and not force eye contact
Insist the resident look the aide in the eye
Report the resident for poor communication

questions.explanation: **Correct (B):** Eye-contact customs vary by culture; the aide recognizes the behavior as a cultural norm, respects it, and does not force eye contact. Why the others are wrong: **A** assuming rudeness misjudges a cultural difference; **C** insisting on eye contact disrespects the resident's customs; **D** reporting the resident treats a cultural norm as a problem.

questions.stem: A resident keeps a religious item, such as a rosary or prayer beads, at the bedside. How should the nurse aide handle this item?

options.text: Move it to a drawer because it clutters the table
Treat it with respect, keep it within the resident's reach, and avoid handling it unnecessarily
Throw it away when cleaning the room
Tell the resident religious items are not allowed at the bedside

questions.explanation: **Correct (B):** Religious items are treated with respect, kept within the resident's reach, and handled only as needed, honoring the resident's spiritual practice. Why the others are wrong: **A** moving a meaningful item out of reach disregards its importance; **C** discarding a religious item is disrespectful and a violation of the resident's rights; **D** residents are entitled to keep religious items with them.

questions.stem: A resident speaks very little English and the nurse aide does not speak the resident's language. According to good practice, what is the most appropriate way to communicate important care information?

options.text: Speak louder in English until the resident understands
Use the facility's approved interpreter service or resources, along with gestures and simple visuals
Skip explaining care since the resident cannot understand anyway
Have another resident who is bilingual translate confidential information

questions.explanation: **Correct (B):** Using the facility's approved interpreter service or resources, supported by gestures and simple visuals, allows accurate communication while protecting confidentiality. Why the others are wrong: **A** speaking louder does not overcome a language barrier; **C** skipping explanations denies the resident information and dignity; **D** using another resident as an interpreter breaches confidentiality and may be inaccurate.

questions.stem: A resident who uses a hearing aid says they cannot hear well today. The nurse aide checks the device. Which simple cause should the aide check for and address or report?

options.text: Whether the hearing aid is turned on, the battery works, and the earmold is clean and free of wax
Whether the resident's eyeglasses are smudged
Whether the room is painted a calming color
Whether the television remote needs new batteries

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** Common, fixable causes of poor hearing-aid function include the device being off, a dead battery, or a wax-clogged earmold; the aide checks these and reports persistent problems. Why the others are wrong: **B** smudged eyeglasses affect vision, not hearing; **C** wall color has no effect on hearing; **D** the television remote is unrelated to the resident's hearing aid.

questions.stem: A nurse aide notices a change in a resident and must report it to the nurse. Which two pieces of information make the report accurate and useful? (Select two.)

options.text: Exactly what was observed and when it occurred
The aide's personal opinion about which medication the resident needs
Objective details such as measurements or the resident's exact words
Gossip about the resident's family heard from another aide

questions.explanation: **Correct (A, C):** An accurate report states exactly what was observed and when, with objective details such as measurements or the resident's own words. Why the others are wrong: **B** recommending a specific medication is outside the aide's scope and is opinion, not observation; **D** unverified gossip is not factual reporting and breaches professionalism.

questions.stem: A resident wants to file a complaint (grievance) about the quality of meals. What is the nurse aide's appropriate response regarding the resident's rights?

options.text: Tell the resident that complaining is not allowed
Support the resident's right to voice a grievance and report it through the proper channel without fear of retaliation
Warn the resident that complaining will lead to worse treatment
Ignore the complaint and change the subject

questions.explanation: **Correct (B):** Residents have the right to voice grievances and have them addressed without retaliation; the aide supports this and reports the concern appropriately. Why the others are wrong: **A** residents are entitled to make complaints; **C** threatening worse treatment is retaliation and a rights violation; **D** ignoring the grievance denies the resident's right to be heard.

questions.stem: A married couple living in the same facility wishes to spend private time together in one room. How should the nurse aide respect this?

options.text: Tell them privacy between residents is not permitted
Support their right to privacy and association, such as by knocking and ensuring they are not disturbed unnecessarily
Enter the room repeatedly without knocking
Report the couple for wanting time alone

questions.explanation: **Correct (B):** Residents have the right to privacy and to associate with whom they choose; the aide knocks, provides privacy, and avoids unnecessary interruptions. Why the others are wrong: **A** residents are entitled to private time and association; **C** entering repeatedly without knocking violates privacy; **D** there is nothing to report—wanting time together is a protected right.

questions.stem: Which two actions are examples of verbal or psychological abuse that a nurse aide must never do and must report if witnessed? (Select two.)

options.text: Threatening or yelling at a resident to make them comply
Calling a resident a demeaning name or mocking them
Explaining a procedure calmly before performing it
Offering the resident a choice of activities

questions.explanation: **Correct (A, B):** Threatening or yelling at a resident and using demeaning names or mockery are forms of verbal and psychological abuse that are prohibited and must be reported. Why the others are wrong: **C** calmly explaining a procedure is respectful, appropriate care; **D** offering choices supports autonomy and dignity, the opposite of abuse.

questions.stem: A nurse aide is asked by a coworker to log in to the electronic health record using the coworker's password to chart for them. What is the correct response?

options.text: Use the coworker's password since it saves time
Decline; each person charts only under their own login, and passwords are not shared
Write the coworker's password on a sticky note for later
Chart whatever the coworker dictates under the coworker's name

questions.explanation: **Correct (B):** Documentation must be done under one's own login, and passwords are kept confidential and never shared, preserving accountability and record integrity. Why the others are wrong: **A** charting under someone else's login falsifies who provided or recorded care; **C** writing down a password breaches security; **D** entering documentation under another person's name misrepresents the record.

questions.stem: A nurse aide takes a photo of a resident on a personal phone to share a 'funny moment' with friends. Why is this a violation?

options.text: It is acceptable as long as the resident's name is not mentioned
It violates the resident's confidentiality and dignity; residents may not be photographed or posted without proper consent
It is fine because the aide owns the phone
It is only a problem if the photo is blurry

questions.explanation: **Correct (B):** Photographing or posting a resident without proper consent breaches confidentiality and dignity and is a serious ethical and legal violation. Why the others are wrong: **A** omitting the name does not make an unauthorized image acceptable; **C** owning the phone does not grant the right to capture a resident's image; **D** image quality is irrelevant to the privacy violation.

questions.stem: A nurse asks the nurse aide to start an intravenous (IV) line for a resident. What is the correct response?

options.text: Start the IV to be a helpful team member
Politely explain that starting an IV is outside the nurse aide's scope of practice and cannot be accepted
Try the IV once and stop if it does not work
Ask a visitor to start the IV instead

questions.explanation: **Correct (B):** A delegated task must be within the aide's legal scope; starting an IV is a nursing task outside the aide's scope, so the aide respectfully declines. Why the others are wrong: **A** willingness does not authorize an out-of-scope, potentially harmful task; **C** attempting an IV at all exceeds the aide's scope; **D** asking a visitor to perform a clinical procedure is unsafe and inappropriate.

questions.stem: Several members of the care team—nurses, therapists, dietary staff, and the nurse aide—meet about a resident's plan of care. What is the nurse aide's most valuable contribution to this team?

options.text: Detailed daily observations of the resident's function, intake, mood, and changes
A medical diagnosis of the resident's condition
A new medication order for the resident
Personal opinions about which residents are favorites

questions.explanation: **Correct (A):** Because the aide spends the most time at the bedside, their detailed observations of function, intake, mood, and any changes are a key contribution to the interdisciplinary team. Why the others are wrong: **B** diagnosing is outside the aide's scope; **C** ordering medications is a provider's role, not the aide's; **D** favoritism is unprofessional and has no place in care planning.

flashcards.back: Hand hygiene. Washing hands (or using alcohol-based hand rub) before and after every resident contact is the single most effective way to prevent the spread of infection.

Treat the blood and body fluids of EVERY resident as potentially infectious, regardless of diagnosis. Use gloves and other PPE whenever contact with blood, body fluids, mucous membranes, or non-intact skin is likely.
Rescue anyone in immediate danger, Activate the alarm, Confine the fire (close doors), Extinguish if small/safe or Evacuate. Rescue comes first.
Keep a wide base of support, bend at the knees and hips (not the waist), lift with the strong leg muscles, keep the load close to your body, and never twist while lifting.
Objective data are observable/measurable (e.g., pulse 96, a reddened area). Subjective data are what the resident reports and you cannot see (e.g., 'I feel dizzy,' pain rated 7/10).

flashcards.front: Dressing a resident with a weak/affected side
flashcards.back: Dress the weak (affected) side FIRST and undress it LAST. This reduces strain on the impaired limb and makes dressing easier.
Reposition bed-bound residents at least every 2 hours, keep skin clean and dry, keep linens smooth and wrinkle-free, and report any new non-blanching reddened area to the nurse.

flashcards.front: Indwelling urinary catheter drainage bag placement
flashcards.back: Keep the drainage bag BELOW the level of the bladder and off the floor so urine drains by gravity and does not flow back toward the bladder, which would raise infection risk.
Residents may refuse any treatment or care. Respect the refusal, try to learn why, offer it again later if appropriate, and report it to the nurse. Never force care or chart care that was not given.
Restraints require a physician's order and are a last resort. A nurse aide never applies a restraint on personal judgment; instead use alternatives, supervise, and report the behavior to the nurse.
Nurse aides are mandatory reporters. Any suspected abuse, neglect, or mistreatment of a resident must be reported to the nurse or supervisor IMMEDIATELY—never ignored or delayed.
An aide works under the nurse's supervision, follows the care plan, observes and reports. Aides do NOT diagnose, prescribe or give medications, perform sterile procedures, or change the care plan.
